review_story.summary: A deadpan walkthrough of an absurd automation that runs a man's whole day, told as a fast list where every item gets its own diagram or fake screenshot.
review_story.hook: 0 to 4 s: the presenter is already mid-sentence with the full workflow floating above his head, then names it. The viewer sees the finished system before any explanation.
highlights: Every claim gets a picture within about a second: 12 of 29 shots are a split with the proof on top and the presenter below, so the joke lands without leaving his face
The layout changes at almost every cut (wide, split, full-frame graphic), so a one-minute list never holds one look for more than a few seconds
One diagram is reused all the way through: each step is another branch of the same workflow, which makes a list feel like one system
Captions are one or two words in heavy italic capitals, placed at the seam of the split, so they read on both layouts
